claim: Prompted intrinsic self-correction (no oracle, no tool) does not raise reasoning accuracy and often lowers it on GSM8K, CommonSenseQA, HotpotQA for GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4-Turbo, Llama-2 (e.g. GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 over two rounds; GPT-3.5 CSQA 75.8 to 38.1). Boundary: see K19 for a dissent.
agent_test: Run the revise step with no external signal vs no revise at equal tokens; log accuracy before/after and right-to-wrong vs wrong-to-right counts.
audit_note: Huang tables and Kamoi survey verified; note GPT-3.5 CSQA 75.8 to 38.1 is the first round, not second, and sources are one empirical paper plus a survey that cites it.

claim: Published gains of RCI and Reflexion-style loops on reasoning partly came from oracle labels deciding when to stop; with the oracle, GPT-3.5 GSM8K goes 75.9 to 84.3 and CSQA 75.8 to 89.7, and the gain vanishes without it. An oracle stop is not self-correction.
agent_test: Never let code holding the gold answer decide revision in our tests; audit every scaffold test for leaked stop signals.
audit_note: Huang oracle numbers (84.3, 89.7) verified; Kim RCI paper stops on ground-truth match; Kamoi flags RCI and Reflexion oracle use (Kamoi largely repeats Huang's point).

claim: Self-correction fails mainly at finding the error, not at fixing it: GPT-4 locates the first wrong step with only 52.87 accuracy (best prompt) on BIG-Bench Mistake, but fixing with the true location helps far more than it harms.
agent_test: Split the revise step into locate and fix; measure locate accuracy against planted errors, then fix accuracy given the true location.
audit_note: Tyen: GPT-4 52.87 best, oracle-location backtracking gains far exceed losses; ProcessBench is consistent.

claim: A model is a poor verifier of its own output on planning and constraint problems: GPT-4 accepted 2 of 100 optimal colourings; 84% of invalid Blocksworld plans were accepted. Self-critique loops scored 1/100 (colouring) and 55/100 vs sound-verifier 88/100 (Blocksworld).
agent_test: Compare LLM-verifier vs sound-checker feedback on a task with an exact checker; report verifier false-positive rate.
audit_note: Numbers verified (2 of 100 optimal colourings accepted, 1/100 self-critique, 84.45% false positives, 55 vs 88/100), but both papers are from the same lab (Stechly/Valmeekam/Kambhampati), so the two domains count as one source group.

claim: With a sound external verifier, the content of the feedback matters little: binary pass/fail was close to full error text (colouring about 40% in all variants; Blocksworld binary 37/50 vs 43/50 with first error). The gain may be resampling plus a check, not critique.
agent_test: Test a bare pass/fail retry against a critique-and-fix retry at equal tokens when a checker exists.
audit_note: Binary vs richer feedback results (colouring ~40% in all variants, Blocksworld 37/50 vs 43/50) verified, but both come from the same Kambhampati-lab papers, and colouring plain top-n sampling also reaches 40%.

claim: In the colouring task a sound verifier gave about 40%, equal to plain top-n sampling (n=15) at 40%, so verified backprompting did not beat best-of-n at similar sample counts. Counterpoint with real tests: Self-Debug on Spider (Codex) matched the 16-sample baseline from one greedy sample plus one debug turn, and from 8 samples beat 32 samples; one turn was enough (gain after turn 1 within 0.1%).
agent_test: Run best-of-n with the same call count as the baseline for every revise loop.

claim: Tool or execution feedback (code interpreter, unit tests, search) often gives gains in correction loops, though uneven: CRITIC adds about 7.7 F1 on QA and 7.0 points on math for ChatGPT; Self-Debug up to +12 with unit tests (+2-3 on Spider without them); Reflexion HumanEval 91.0 vs 80.1 but MBPP 77.1 vs 80.1.
agent_test: Give the revise step a real execution or check result vs none; same token budget.
audit_note: Figures verified (CRITIC +7.7 F1 and +7.0 math, Self-Debug up to +12, Reflexion HumanEval 91.0 vs 80.1) but 'reliable gains' is too strong: Self-Debug gains are +2-3 on Spider, Reflexion trails GPT-4 on MBPP (77.1 vs 80.1), and Olausson shows self-repair gains are modest and uneven per compute budget.
claim_before_audit: Tool or execution feedback (code interpreter, unit tests, search) gives reliable gains in correction loops: CRITIC adds about 7.7 F1 on QA and 7.0 points on math for ChatGPT; Self-Debug up to +12 with unit tests; Reflexion HumanEval 91 vs 80.

claim: The tool is not always the cause: for ChatGPT on GSM8K, CRITIC without tool (78.2, +5.7) beat CRITIC with tool (77.0, +4.5); on text-davinci-003 the no-tool variant lost 1.8. Tool necessity is model-dependent.
agent_test: Replicate on our model: critique with and without an executable check on math, several seeds.

claim: Self-repair of code, with cost counted in tokens, gives modest and uneven gains against drawing more fresh samples; feedback quality is the bottleneck (human explanations 52.6% repair success vs GPT-4 self-explanations 33.3%).
agent_test: Fresh sampling vs repair at equal token budget on code tasks with tests.
audit_note: Olausson verified (1.05x, 0.97x, 33.3% to 52.6%); Self-Debug and Kamoi consistent but Olausson is the sole source of the numbers.

claim: Self-Refine gains concentrate on style, preference and constraint-coverage tasks (sentiment 43.2 vs 0 without feedback; dialogue 25.4 to 74.6) and are about zero on math (GPT-4 92.9 to 93.1) because the critic says 'looks good' 94% of the time.
agent_test: Run revise only when the task spec lists checkable constraints; skip on single-answer reasoning unless a check exists.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Part of Self-Refine's reported gain comes from a weak first prompt: on CommonGen-Hard, a first prompt with the requirement gives 81.8 and self-correction then lowers it to 75.1, versus Madaan's 44.0 to 67.0.
agent_test: Always compare against the strongest first-attempt prompt before crediting revision.
audit_note: Huang table verified (44.0 to 67.0 Madaan; 81.8 to 75.1 improved prompt); Kamoi survey flags weak first prompt in Self-Refine but is derivative of Huang.

claim: Multi-agent debate is mostly a voting effect: same prompt, full GSM8K test set, debate 83.2 and 83.0 vs self-consistency 85.3 and 88.2 at matched response counts (6 and 9), GPT-3.5.
agent_test: Compare any multi-pass critique with majority voting at the same call count.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Models show a self-correction blind spot: the same injected error is fixed when presented as the user's but missed when in the model's own prior turn (64.5% average blind spot over 14 open non-reasoning models). Appending 'Wait' cuts it by 89.3%.
agent_test: Re-present own earlier output as an external draft in the check step vs as 'your previous answer'; add a 'Wait' cue; compare.

claim: Reasoning-trained models close the blind spot almost as well as a 'Wait' cue on a base model (DeepSeek-V3 0.902 with Wait vs 0.908 reasoning; Qwen3-32B 0.793 vs 0.894). Self-checking is partly an activation problem, cheap to elicit.
agent_test: Append a short continue-checking cue before the final answer vs none at equal tokens.

claim: Budget forcing with 'Wait' extends thinking and raises accuracy slightly (s1-32B AIME24 50.0 to 56.7, MATH500 92.6 to 93.0), small benchmarks.
agent_test: Test an appended re-check cue as a token-matched alternative to a separate critique call.

claim: Training can make intrinsic self-correction positive: SCoRe (multi-turn RL) lifts Gemini 1.5 Flash MATH500 accuracy at try 2 from 41.4 (base) to 64.4, with right-to-wrong falling from 15.8% to 1.4%; RISE gives +17.7 to +23.9 on GSM8K for 7B models; prompted baselines and plain SFT do not. Not available to a scaffold-only agent.
agent_test: Out of scope for the scaffold; use as an upper reference only.
audit_note: SCoRe (41.4 to 64.4, 15.8% to 1.4%) and RISE (+17.7, +23.9 GSM8K) verified in full texts; 'not available to scaffold-only agent' is an inference.

claim: Fine-tuned gains are partly oracle-assisted: RISE headline numbers use oracle early stop; and the SCoRe paper's text says base fix rate 9.5% while its table says 4.6%.
agent_test: Do not use RISE headline numbers as a no-oracle figure.

claim: Flip behaviour is the main mechanism of harm: models change correct answers to wrong ones more than the reverse (GPT-3.5 keeps its first answer 74.7% on GSM8K; base Gemini changes 15.8% right to wrong vs 4.6% wrong to right); GPT-3.5 changes answers more than 6 times in 81.3% of 10-round chats. 2025-26 check: a neutral 'are you sure' round still overturned correct answers in o1-mini, 4o, DeepSeek V3 and R1 (Zhang). At T=0 with a plain revise prompt, correct-to-wrong stays small on checkable tasks (SAT 0.0 to 2.1%) but reaches 13.25% on BBEH/HLE, and the strongest model (Gemini Pro on HLE) fixes 10.56% vs breaks 9.32% (Stav).
agent_test: Log right-to-wrong and wrong-to-right counts at every revise step; add a keep-unless-evidence rule and test it.
audit_note: Verified: Huang 74.7%, Kumar 15.8% vs 4.6%, Zhang 81.3% >6 changes and are-you-sure on o1-mini/4o/V3/R1, Stav C2W at most 2.1% on SAT up to 13.25% and Gemini Pro HLE 10.56 vs 9.32; Zhang tasks are Yes/No and agent tasks, and 'main mechanism' is the authors' interpretation.

claim: Dissent: with zero temperature and unbiased prompts, small gains appear in all tested models (GPT-4 MMLU 83.66 to 84.76; CSQA GPT-3.5 75.92 to 76.00; HotpotQA GPT-3.5 31 to 47), but most effects are under 1 point, samples small (first 200), no error bars.
agent_test: Replicate with several seeds and error bars: neutral prompt plus temperature 0 revise vs no revise.

claim: Confidence-conditioned prompts ('keep your answer if very confident, otherwise update', If-or-Else) mostly cancel the loss caused by Huang's critical prompt, but add only about 1 to 3 points over no revision. GSM8K-100 GPT-3.5: critique hurts confident answers (82.75 to 77.35) and helps unconfident ones (27.69 to 39.23). 5-set average: GPT-3.5-0613 standard 70.3, critical 66.1, IoE 73.0; GPT-4 85.1, 82.5, 86.6. Single run, no error bars, 2023-24 models.
agent_test: Keep-if-confident wording in the check step vs neutral wording, 5+ seeds, on a reasoning model; log right-to-wrong and wrong-to-right counts.

claim: Detecting errors in LLM output is hard: strong detectors have low recall and are prompt-sensitive; ProcessBench shows reasoning models detect step errors much better (o1-mini F1 87.9 vs GPT-4o 61.9).
agent_test: Use a reasoning-grade model for the check step vs a base model at equal tokens.
audit_note: ReaLMistake abstract (low recall, prompt sensitivity) and ProcessBench (o1-mini 87.9 vs GPT-4o 61.9, 3,400 cases) verified; ProcessBench is step-level math errors, not the same task as ReaLMistake.

claim: Prompted self-correction is useful when verification is much easier than generation and the answer splits into independently checkable parts (Chain-of-Verification FACTSCORE 55.9 to 71.4; Wikidata lists 17% to 70% when each item is verified in isolation from the draft). Transfer to multi-step reasoning is mixed: in DISC's reimplementation on BIG-Bench Mistake (Sonnet 4.5), CoVe broke 28.9% of correct multistep arithmetic answers and 35.6% on word sorting, while for GPT-4o it was best on arithmetic (95.0 vs DISC 54.0).
agent_test: Verify claims item by item in isolation from the draft vs whole-draft critique.

claim: Self-improvement depends on the generation-verification gap, which grows with pre-training compute for some verifiers and saturates within 2-3 rounds; on easy-to-check Sudoku most models still fail to self-improve.
agent_test: Measure our model's generation-verification gap on the task before adding a revise loop; cap rounds at 2.

claim: The R1-Zero 'aha moment' of RL-learned reflection is disputed: base models already emit reflection words and reflection frequency is not positively correlated with accuracy.
agent_test: Count reflection phrases vs accuracy in our own traces; do not reward reflection words.

claim: Small models need a strong verifier to self-correct: small LMs learn self-correction only with correct-solution-guided critiques.
agent_test: Not testable at scaffold level; note for open-model fallback.

claim: Reflection memory helps retries only with an external pass/fail signal, and a wrong signal costs: plain retries solved none of the trial-1 failures on HotPotQA while Reflexion did; but the model-written test signal had a 16.3% false-positive rate on MBPP Python (FP 0.16, FN 0.59), and Reflexion (0.77) fell below the no-loop GPT-4 baseline (0.80). On HumanEval (FP 0.01) it rose 0.80 to 0.91. With imperfect tests, resampling has a ceiling, and the best number of tries is about 5 at a cost ratio of 4 (Stroebl).
agent_test: Retry with stored reflection vs bare retry at equal calls, with a test as gate.
audit_note: Reflexion table (HumanEval 0.80/0.91 FP 0.01; MBPP 0.80/0.77 FP 0.16 FN 0.59; 16.3% vs 1.4%), HotPotQA no-retry-gains baselines, and Stroebl K about 5 at ratio 4 all verified in full texts.

claim: Equal-token test for a reasoning model: on Qwen3-4B, giving the first solve a larger budget (8,192 tokens) matched the best verify-after-solve policy (MATH500 76.0 vs 76.3; GSM8K 94.54 vs 94.47) with 28% fewer total tokens on MATH500 and no second call. Always-verify added 2.2% harmful flips; gated verify cut them to 1.0%. Much of the MATH500 fix was finishing truncated attempts (45.4% truncated at 4,096).
agent_test: Compare 'check call' vs 'same tokens on a longer first solve' on 2025-26 reasoning models, 3+ seeds, with truncation handled. Default: tune first-solve budget, then gate the check.

claim: Refinement can beat plain resampling for weak non-reasoning models when followed by a vote (N=8, D=4: Qwen2.5-1.5B average 25.67 vs Maj@8 13.21 and reward-model best-of-8 14.95), but it spends more compute than those baselines, so it is not an equal-compute win. For a stronger model the gain over a reward-model baseline drops to +2.36.
agent_test: Vote over checked drafts vs vote over raw drafts at equal total tokens.

claim: A fine-tuned revision model beats best-of-N at equal generation count, and the best sequential/parallel mix needs up to 4x less compute (PaLM 2-S*, MATH), but only with trained revision and a verifier or vote over the revision chain; naive use converts about 38% of correct answers to wrong.
agent_test: Prompt-only agents must add a selector (vote or check) after any revision.
audit_note: Snell verified: up to 4x less test-time compute than best-of-N, about 38% of correct answers flipped to wrong by the revision model, verifier or sequential majority vote needed; S2R/Kamoi support the training-dependence.

claim: No prompt-only method matched the gain of trained self-correction. Training (S2R: Qwen2.5-Math-7B MATH500 51.0 to 81.6 with 3.1k samples) beats prompting, but long-CoT SFT of similar size reaches 80.2, so the self-check structure itself adds little (+1.4). Kamoi's survey (2024) finds no fair prompted success in general tasks. Gap 10 stays open for 2025-26 open models.
agent_test: Do not plan to drop external signals; keep S5 tied to checkers.
audit_note: S2R verified (51.0 to 81.6 with 3.1k samples; equal-amount long-CoT SFT 80.2); Kamoi abstract supports no fair prompted success up to May 2024; the +1.4 is a single-run difference.

claim: A cheap first-wrong-step locator needs a reasoning-trained model: ProcessBench average F1 o1-mini 87.9 vs GPT-4o 61.9 (3,400 cases). Whether locate-then-fix beats one-shot critique at equal tokens with a 2025 model is not tested.
agent_test: Test a locate step on a reasoning model vs one-shot critique at equal tokens.

claim: A neutral 'are you sure' refinement round hurts correct answers in current models, and 10-round chats make answers flip repeatedly (GPT-3.5: 81.3% changed more than 6 times in 10 rounds; Llama-3.1-8B -20.4 points, 58.8% of correct answers overturned). Re-attaching the original question at the end of the refinement prompt gave +3.2 to +4.9 ACC and 5.3 to 10.9 points fewer overturned answers. With a judge gate, iteration plateaus by K=3 (net +22 at K=1, +34 at K=3, +35 at K=8) and degradation does not compound; without the gate, I:D falls 2 to 4x.
agent_test: Cap rounds at 1 ungated, at most 3 gated; end every check prompt with the task restated.

claim: Checker independence matters: in DISC a different, stronger verifier and judge fixed gpt-4.1-nano outputs far more (54.0 to 71.6, +34 net) than gpt-5.2 checking itself (75.3 to 79.3, +8 net); the strong verifier found 51 errors in nano's outputs vs 18 in its own. Capability is confounded with independence, so this is not a test of the attribution framing.
agent_test: If one model only: fresh context, draft as external text; test against a neutral-style rewritten draft (Panickssery: GPT-4 recognises its own text 73.5%).

claim: The attribution (blind-spot) effect is stated by its author as a conversational-role effect, not authorship: the only cue that differs is the chat role header, with off-policy injected errors. A scaffold that pastes the draft into a user message may already be in the 'external' condition. No test at equal tokens, no scaffold test, and the 2026 spectral-theory follow-up adds no data.
agent_test: A/B: draft in assistant turn vs draft in user turn labelled as another solver's, equal tokens, math and code, 5+ seeds.

claim: Where a cheap sound check exists, intrinsic revision pays: SAT revision at T=0: Mistral 34.62 to 64.96, Haiku 4.5 75.64 to 93.59, DeepSeek V3.1 78.63 to 92.74, with correct-to-wrong at most 2.1%. Code with real tests: Self-Debug MBPP Codex 61.4 to 69.4, GPT-4 72.8 to 80.6; TransCoder GPT-4 77.3 to 88.8. Without execution the code gain shrinks to about +3 to +5 points and for MBPP Codex simple feedback is below baseline (57.6 vs 61.4). No study compares check-and-fix with best-of-n at equal calls on a 2025 model.
agent_test: Route S5 to code with tests, recomputable arithmetic, constraint lists. Elsewhere gate or skip.
audit_note: Stav SAT numbers, Self-Debug 61.4 to 69.4, 72.8 to 80.6, TransCoder 77.3 to 88.8 and Stroebl are right, but 'without execution the code gain vanishes' is too strong: without execution MBPP gains shrink (Codex simple 57.6 vs 61.4 but +Expl 64.4 and +Trace 66.2; GPT-4 76.0 to 76.4 vs 72.8; TransCoder Codex 83.4-83.9 vs 80.4).
claim_before_audit: Where a cheap sound check exists, intrinsic revision pays: SAT revision at T=0: Mistral 34.62 to 64.96, Haiku 4.5 75.64 to 93.59, DeepSeek V3.1 78.63 to 92.74, with correct-to-wrong at most 2.1%. Code with real tests: Self-Debug MBPP Codex 61.4 to 69.4, GPT-4 72.8 to 80.6; TransCoder GPT-4 77.3 to 88.8. Without execution the code gain vanishes (MBPP Codex simple 57.6 vs 61.4). No study compares check-and-fix with best-of-n at equal calls on a 2025 model.

claim: Verify-then-select over many drafts beats plain voting: Gemini 1.5 Pro Verification@200 vs Consistency@200: AIME 8/15 vs 4/15, MATH 467 vs 460 of 500, LiveBench Math 135 vs 118 of 200, LiveBench Reasoning 97 vs 75 of 140 (single run per cell). Frontier models verify poorly out of the box; comparing across drafts helps locate errors.
agent_test: Compare across 2+ drafts instead of checking one; measure at equal total calls.
